summary: This class defines a decorated cookie that builds on the general Cookie class, reusing its flavor field and constructor while supplying its own description.

lines.text: The extends keyword makes DecoratedCookie a subclass of Cookie, so every field and method already written in Cookie is available here without being retyped.
This hands the flavor up to the Cookie constructor so the parent class does the work of storing it — the pre-bundled starter kit you then add to.
This annotation states the intent to replace a method inherited from Cookie, and the compiler will complain if no such method exists, catching typos in the method name or parameters.
Because the subclass supplies its own describe(), a decorated cookie can report its own details without Cookie needing an if/else chain for every cookie variety.

lines.code: return "This " + getFlavor() + " cookie is decorated with sprinkles and icing!";
lines.text: The flavor field is private to Cookie, so even a subclass reads it through the inherited getter rather than touching the field directly.
